title: Cinematic language and style
description:
## Background
Shot selection, movement, composition, background, perspective, mood and one consistent style per film (human notes, round 1).

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed; boards show the cinematic choices and the style profile.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md (draft 3), section 7a.

title: Define style profiles and four example profiles
description:
## Background
Every film keeps one look. A style profile limits every shot choice, and any break from it needs a stated reason. examples/child-peek already has an informal profile (quiet-evening-storybook), written inline in story.json.

## Task
- Add a style-profile record (envelope kind "style-profile"). It covers framing habits, angle and lens habits, movement (for storyboard films: holds, parallax drifts and push-ins), tonal key and contrast, light, palette, editing rhythm and aspect ratio. Each field lists preferred and avoided values.
- The profile also specifies the drawn look, limited to what the renderer can draw: paper, ink, two or three fill values, line widths, wobble, detail simplification, and hatching (character layer only; the mannequin is never hatched). A signature choice that can't be drawn, such as a colour grade or film grain, gets a drawable substitute agreed at approval 1.
- Write five profiles, described by traits rather than by director names: quiet-evening-storybook (moved out of child-peek's story.json, which then refers to it by id), symmetrical tableau, colour-field epic, Hong Kong police thriller, and black-and-white noir.
- Shots take their choices from the profile first, then the camera setup, then any shot override. Each shot gives one reason for its choices, and any departure from the profile gives its own reason.
- Approval 1 pins a style reference strip (one wide, one close, one insert) by hash.

## Acceptance criteria
- All five profiles validate.
- Each profile renders a three-shot sample sequence, and the five sequences look clearly different in framing, movement and key.
- child-peek refers to its profile by id.

## Tests
Schema fixtures; the human reviews the five sample sequences.

## Context
Schemas come from am-e-contract-tnm.1. The value pass (am-00y.2) draws the tonal key.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7a.6

title: Support authored diagram and annotated-detail inserts as boards
description:
## Background
For an explainer-type beat, an authored diagram can be cheaper than staging a scene. The storyboard stories in phases A and B don't need this, so it is not on their path.

## Task
Let a shot supply an authored SVG (a diagram or an annotated detail) as its board and final still. The SVG carries a source digest, evidence for any claim it makes, the style profile id and a must-see test. It goes through the same animatic and approval as a drawn board.

## Acceptance criteria
A test diagram plays in the animatic and passes the phone review protocol. The test is a side-on sketch of a camera, a hand, and the body between them.

## Tests
Schema fixture; render check.

## Context
The shot record is in am-e-contract-tnm.1; style profiles are in am-00y.1.

## Plan reference
Plan section 4, step 5

title: Character sheets: turn posed mannequins into sketched characters
description:
## Background
Viewers follow people, not mannequins. A character sheet turns a posed mannequin into a recognisable sketched character that looks the same in every shot. There are two layers. The mannequin has no fingers, no spiky hair, no hatching and no clothed form. The character layer adds hairstyle, garments, fingers, face and hatching, drawn consistently. This bead covers silhouette, garments and hair. Fingers, faces and expressions come after the hands-and-faces spike (am-00y.13), in am-00y.15.

## Task
- Add a character-sheet record: identity, body profile (one of lib/pose/profiles.json), silhouette shapes, garments as forms, a value per garment, signature props, a face option, and named expressions (filled in later).
- Render a character layer on the posed figure: the character's real hairstyle (spiky included), headwear as a simple solid, and coats, sleeves and skirts lofted on the body's own forms, so they move with the pose. Garment values feed the value pass (am-00y.2). Hatching follows the style profile.
- Render a turnaround per character: front, three-quarter, side, back and one action pose.
- Figures without a sheet render exactly as today.

## Acceptance criteria
- A fresh viewer can tell two characters in one frame apart at thumbnail size.
- A coat hangs and moves correctly with the pose in front, side and back views.
- Hair, garments and hatching are drawn in the same style in every turnaround view and every shot.
- The golden tests are unchanged for figures without a sheet.

## Tests
Golden turnarounds; schema fixtures.

## Context
Renderer: lib/pose/mannequin.js. Mannequin conventions are in AGENTS.md (Storyboard conventions). Needs the per-render context (am-e-board-1wg.3) and several figures in one frame (am-e-board-1wg.6).

## Plan reference
Plan section 7b

title: Export boards as cutout layers by depth
description:
## Background
Movement in storyboard films is parallax, so each board has to be split into depth layers. Phase A can use one board split by hand. This bead is the reusable exporter for phase B.

## Task
- Render a board as separate transparent layers: background (drawn complete, including whatever figures and props hide), midground set, each figure, and foreground props.
- Write the layer manifest that the parallax step reads (format defined in am-e-asm-qgh.5): canvas size, artwork in order by digest, origins, and depth from the scene record.
- Split a rail or limb where the front-to-back order changes along it. Parts that touch share one transform.
- Paper, frame marks and captions stay fixed in delivery space and are not layers.
- If a board can't be separated cleanly, report it and fall back to holding the board still.

## Acceptance criteria
- With zero offset, stacking the layers reproduces the inked board exactly.
- The background has no holes where the cutouts were.

## Tests
A flatten-and-compare test on the child-peek sh2 board and the balcony-lean scene.

## Context
Scenes: examples/child-peek/scenes/, resource/pose/balcony-lean.json.

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7a.3 and 8 (row 3b)

title: Try code-drawn hands and faces, then decide
description:
## Background
Code-drawn fingers and faces tend to look stiff. The human decides after seeing real attempts.

## Task
In the character layer of one character sheet, draw fingers (posed from the three hand types: open, fist and V) and simple faces: oval heads with features placed on the two face-direction curves. Show the turnaround plus three or four story poses, side by side with the mannequin. The human then chooses: keep the code drawing, or have an image model redraw hands and faces over the board.

## Acceptance criteria
The human's decision is recorded on this bead and in plan section 7b.

## Tests
None; this is a decision spike.

## Context
The character layer comes from am-00y.11. The decision is carried out by am-00y.15.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7b

title: Analyse the microdrama skill package for ideas to adopt
Draw fingers, faces and expressions in the character layer
description:
## Background
The hands-and-faces spike (am-00y.13) decides whether fingers and faces are drawn by code or redrawn by an image model over the board. This bead carries out that decision.

## Task
- Fingers posed from the three hand types (open, fist, V), drawn the same way in every shot.
- Facial features on the oval head along the two face-direction curves.
- Named expressions from a small vocabulary (neutral, concern, surprise, fear, relief, amusement, sadness, anger), drawn in the same face proportions, chosen per shot with an onset, and resolved after gaze and head turn.
- The mannequin itself still has no fingers or features.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fingers and faces are identical in style across all turnaround views and every shot.
- A fresh viewer names the expression in four of five test boards.

## Tests
Golden turnarounds; expression fixtures.

## Context
If the spike chooses an image model, this bead becomes the adapter and consistency check instead; rewrite it then.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7b

title: Draw a light-versus-dark value pass on boards
description:
## Background
Line art alone can't show mood, and light versus dark is the main way to control it. The child-peek boards are line only, so blue hour, the warm window and the headlights don't read.

## Task
- Add a two- or three-tone shadow block-in: flat greys over the paper, in the sketch style, driven by the shot's tonal key (high, mid or low) and its light motivation (window, lamp, streetlight, headlights, sun at a time of day).
- A high-key board is mostly paper. A low-key board is mostly dark, with the subject picked out. A silhouette is drawn as a flat dark shape.
- Light sources can glow: a lit window, a streetlight pool, a headlight beam as a lighter wedge.
- With no key set, output is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- High-key, low-key and silhouette versions of one scene read as different moods at phone size, and the figure stays readable in all three.
- The child-peek boards show a warm window behind Mia against a darker street, and the headlight beam in sh3.

## Tests
Golden renders of the three keys; existing goldens unchanged when no key is set.

## Context
Renderer: lib/pose/mannequin.js. Boards: examples/child-peek/scenes/sh1-sh5.json. Cast shadows and real light directions are a later bead (am-e-board-1wg.5).

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7a.3 and 8 (row 3a)

title: Add keyframed 3D camera paths (after phase B)
description:
## Background
Camera movement (dolly, pan, tilt, crane, push-in) is a shot choice and has to be judged in time. Storyboard films use holds and parallax only, so real camera paths wait until a story needs them, after phase B.

## Task
- Add an optional camera path to scene v2: keyframes of position, look-at and field of view over frames, with easing. Each move records the visible result it must produce.
- Draw start and end boards with movement arrows. Render in-between frames for the animatic.
- A held still allows only a previewed crop inside its bounds. A reveal behind a foreground object needs a rendered path or a second board.
- Check the reveal frame, and play the move to look for flicker.

## Acceptance criteria
A dolly-in and a zoom from the same start frame visibly differ in perspective, and the animatic plays the move.

## Tests
Path interpolation tests; golden start and end boards.

## Context
Needs the hardened fixed camera (am-e-board-1wg.8).

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7a.3 and 8 (row 3b-later)

title: Composition overlay and framing checks
description:
## Background
Framing should be reviewable by eye and partly checkable by code.

## Task
- Add an optional overlay of thirds grid, safe area and caption band, used on the review sheet (am-e-board-1wg.12) and never on final boards.
- Check subject placement against the shot's stated composition, headroom and lead room, and the tonal contrast of the subject against its background.

## Acceptance criteria
A subject placed on a third by a fixed camera lands within tolerance, and missing lead room is flagged.

## Tests
Unit tests on projected bounds.

## Context
The fixed camera exists (camera.verticalFovDeg and frame {w,h} in lib/pose/mannequin.js).

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7a.3 and 8 (row 3c)

title: Check cutting grammar across adjacent shots
description:
## Background
Shots are chosen as a sequence, and some film grammar can be checked from the scene records.

## Task
- Read each shot's continuity record: the axis id (if one is declared), camera side, screen direction, who looks at what, subject side and shot size.
- Between adjacent shots, flag a crossed 180-degree line, a screen-direction or eyeline mismatch, and a change in size too small to read as deliberate.
- Apply axis rules only where an axis is declared. A deliberate break must state its reason. Leave ambiguous axes unscored.
- Project look directions for a shot and its reverse.

## Acceptance criteria
Each rule has a passing and a failing fixture pair.

## Tests
Fixture pairs.

## Context
The continuity record is in am-e-contract-tnm.1.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7a.2

title: Flag shots that drift from the film's style profile
description:
## Background
Consistency of style needs checking, not just intent.

## Task
Compare each shot's cinematic fields with the film's style profile and flag avoided values and unexplained breaks: for example, a handheld shot in a locked-off film, or a high-key shot in a noir.

## Acceptance criteria
Flags appear on the review sheet. A break with a stated reason is shown but not flagged as an error.

## Tests
Fixtures per example profile.

## Context
Profiles come from am-00y.1; the review sheet is am-e-board-1wg.12.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7a.6

title: Build a library of named shot recipes
description:
## Background
The shot step needs starting points, in the same way the figure has reference poses (resource/pose/).

## Task
Write scene records, boards and usage notes for these recipes: establishing wide to insert, over-the-shoulder pair, one-point perspective corridor, low-angle hero, high-angle isolation, silhouette against a window, dolly-in to a realisation, and dolly zoom.

## Acceptance criteria
Every recipe renders, and the human has reviewed each one.

## Tests
Golden renders.

## Context
Needs the value pass (am-00y.2), camera paths (am-00y.3) and environment presets (am-e-board-1wg.4).

## Plan reference
Plan section 7a.5

title: Emphasise the focal subject and story detail; optional perspective guides
description:
## Background
The subject has to read first, and perspective has to be visible.

## Task
- Emphasis follows the focal subject and the story detail. Detail that carries the story keeps its contrast (the rail in the peeking shot). Competing set detail is drawn at a lower line weight and with less detail.
- Optional perspective guides: a faint horizon line and vanishing points from the camera, available on request for review and never on final boards. Horizon placement is treated as a composition choice.

## Acceptance criteria
In two versions of one street view, a fresh viewer finds the designated doorway or figure first.

## Tests
Golden renders.

## Context
Needs environment presets (am-e-board-1wg.4).

## Plan reference
Plan section 8 (row 6a)

title: Choose the style profile for the first storyboard films
description:
## Background
The first films use the sketch itself as the final picture; image generation is deferred to phase E. What's still open is which style profile they use. examples/child-peek has its own informal profile, quiet-evening-storybook, written into its story.json. The four example profiles are symmetrical tableau, colour-field epic, Hong Kong police thriller and black-and-white noir (am-00y.1).

## Task
The human decides. Record the decision as a comment on this bead and in the plan (plan section 13, Q7), then close the bead.

Options: (a) a profile per story; (b) one house profile for the channel, so the films read as a series, allowing small per-film variations. Recommendation: (b), using quiet-evening-storybook as the house profile unless the phase B story asks for something else.

## Acceptance criteria
The decision is recorded in both places.

## Plan reference
plan section 13, Q7

title: Assembly (stage 5)
description:
## Background
Groups the beads for plan section 5.5.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed.

## Reference
docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 5.5.

title: Grow the rough-cut compiler into full assembly
description:
## Background
The phase A compiler (am-mcd.4) only holds stills with hard cuts over a voice track. Phase B needs captions, music, parallax clips and loudness control.

## Task
- Extend the compiler to handle stills and clips, the parallax moves from am-e-asm-qgh.5, crossfades, captions (burned in or as a sidecar file), the music bed, loudness at -16 LUFS integrated with peaks at or below -1 dBTP, and the delivery size from the brief.
- Keep the phase A edit rules: intervals select media by digest and check the bytes; anchors are either speech (a cue plus an offset) or picture (a beat plus a frame).
- Swapping only the selected take keeps the board approval but reopens final approval.

## Acceptance criteria
Size, fps and frame count are correct; duration is within one frame; cuts land on their cue frames; both phase B cuts reproduce offline.

## Tests
A stub media render with decode checks around each cut.

## Context
Also needs asset provenance (am-e-contract-tnm.6) and the platform decision (am-e-pub-5yn.1).

## Plan reference
Plan section 6

title: Pipeline runner with stage receipts and approval checkpoints
description:
## Background
The stages exist separately, but nothing runs them in order or knows which outputs are out of date.

## Task
- Add `node bin/movie.js run <project>`. Per stage, hash the inputs, the code and the tool versions; rebuild only stale outputs; write atomically.
- Stop at the three approvals (script, animatic, final cut). Each approval pins the hashes of what was approved.
- Paid-call reservation (am-e-contract-tnm.4) hooks in only when generation returns in phase E, so it isn't needed here.

## Acceptance criteria
A second run does no work. Changing one shot rebuilds only that shot and the assembly. Changing the title rebuilds only the release.

## Tests
End to end on the example project with stub services; interrupted writes; two concurrent runs.

## Plan reference
Plan section 5.3

title: Cut the approved boards to the narration as an animatic
description:
## Background
Voice comes before visuals. The storyboard is approved as a timed film before any more work is spent on it.

## Task
Using the compiler, hold each board for its shot's span, taken from the word timings, with captions.

## Acceptance criteria
The producer approves the sequence, and the approval pins every board hash.

## Tests
A recut after one changed line reuses the unaffected shots.

## Context
Needs the review sheet (am-e-board-1wg.12), the value pass (am-00y.2), synthesised narration (am-e-voice-fi2.2) and the compiler (am-mcd.4).

## Plan reference
Plan section 4, step 6

title: Frame the same scenes for portrait and landscape
description:
## Background
Landscape explainers come after the vertical films. The same scene records should serve both shapes.

## Task
Add per-delivery camera framing rules, so one scene record yields both a portrait and a landscape board, each composed for its shape rather than letterboxed.

## Acceptance criteria
Both masters look deliberately composed.

## Tests
A visual check of both, rendered from one record.

## Context
Frame size is set per scene with frame {w,h}; the fixed camera uses camera.verticalFovDeg.

## Plan reference
Plan section 3, Q4

title: Animate parallax drifts and push-ins from cutout layers in assembly
description:
## Background
Static boards can feel like a slideshow. Parallax gives a sense of depth at almost no cost.

## Task
- Define the layer manifest: canvas size, ordered layers (artwork path and digest, depth, origin), and per-shot start and end transforms with easing.
- In the compiler, a shot may carry a parallax move: drift direction, push-in amount, duration and easing. Each layer is translated and scaled at a rate set by its depth, with near layers moving more than far ones.
- Moves are capped so that no cutout edge or frame edge ever shows.
- The manifest can be written by hand (phase A: one hand-split board) or by the exporter (am-00y.12, phase B).

## Acceptance criteria
A drift on child-peek sh2 shows the balusters moving faster than the street, with no gaps or exposed edges.

## Tests
Frame checks at the start, middle and end of the move; an edge-exposure check.

## Context
Builds on the phase A compiler (am-mcd.4).

## Plan reference
Plan section 7a.3

title: Storyboard (stage 2)

## Background
Groups the beads for plan section 5.2.

## Success Criteria
All child beads closed.

docs/planning/PLAN_FOR_AI_MOVIE.md, section 5.2.

title: Joint limits on reach targets, named contact sites, structured diagnostics
description:
## Background
Reach targets currently bypass joint limits. Warnings are plain strings, and ladder rungs have no names.

## Task
- Guard ik2 against zero distance and against a pole vector parallel to the limb.
- After solving, compute the achieved angles and check them against the limits.
- Name contact sites (rungs, rails) when props are expanded.
- Emit structured diagnostics: code, figure, joint, requested and achieved values with units, and a suggested fix. The codes are target-outside-workspace, joint-range-exceeded, pole-conflict, contact-distance, prop-intersection and gaze-shortfall. Keep today's warning strings, so the golden manifest still matches.
- A scene that combines `stand` with reach targets is invalid, not repairable.

## Acceptance criteria
A reachable target that needs an impossible elbow is reported with its code. Moving a rung moves its contact sites.

## Tests
Coincident targets; unreachable and too-close limbs; invalid rung spacing.

## Context
lib/pose/mannequin.js: ik2 and the CLAMPS warnings.

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7 (step 5) and 8 (order 4)

title: Annotate the reference poses by action, support and contacts
description:
## Background
Pose retrieval should match on what touches what before it matches on words.

## Task
- Make validated pose-example records for resource/pose/: setup id, support (floor, seat, rail, rung or airborne), contacts [{figure, joint, target}], gaze target, dynamic or static, allowed flexibility, camera sector, occlusion notes and scene hash.
- Two views of one setup share a setup id but stay separate results.
- Retrieval must show that the requested contacts exist in the result.

## Acceptance criteria
Requests for crouching, sitting and peeking, worded in different ways, retrieve the right starting records.

## Tests
Retrieval tests with paraphrased requests, run against the evaluation set (am-e-board-1wg.11).

## Plan reference
Plan section 7, step 2

title: Build an evaluation set of 30 to 50 shot descriptions
description:
## Background
Turning a description into a scene needs a measurable benchmark.

## Task
- Write 30 to 50 varied shot descriptions, each with a human-accepted scene record, covering every support type and camera sector.
- Keep the set apart from the retrieval library. Split by setup or brief family; keep descriptions, solutions and notes out of retrieval and tuning; replace any case that enters the library.
- Report first-pass accepts, accepts after repair, manual blocks, abandoned shots and minutes.

## Acceptance criteria
The set is committed, and the accept rate can be computed automatically.

## Tests
Every record validates and renders cleanly.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7

title: Generate a review sheet showing shots in sequence
description:
## Background
Storyboards are judged in sequence, not frame by frame.

## Task
- Produce an HTML sheet showing each frame at delivery size between its neighbours, with the shot's intent and its must-see list.
- Follow the phone review protocol: the delivery crop, a fixed size, the real caption band, a fixed viewing distance and duration, and a statement of whether sound is on.
- Show the style reference strip, the optional composition overlay (am-00y.4), and flags from the composition, continuity and style-drift checks beside each frame.
- Approval writes each frame's hash into its shot record.

## Acceptance criteria
Changing a scene after approval marks the approval stale.

## Tests
A stale-approval test.

## Context
examples/child-peek/boards.png is today's hand-made contact sheet; the sheet replaces it.

## Plan reference
Plan sections 4 and 7

title: Write the cinematic heuristics guide
description:
## Background
The scene step needs explicit rules for camera height, lens feel and placement.

## Task
Write a short guide that maps the shot vocabulary to camera numbers: size and lens to distance and vertical field of view (camera.verticalFovDeg); angle to camera height and pitch; composition to subject placement in the frame. Cover the common words: low angle, over the shoulder, insert, reverse and point of view.

## Acceptance criteria
A new contributor can predict which camera the scene step will choose.

## Context
It feeds the description-to-scene step (am-e-board-1wg.7) and the shot-list skill (skills/shot-list).

## Plan reference
Plan sections 7 and 7a.1

title: Solve gaze after grounding and measure the final gaze ray
description:
## Background
fig() aims the head at the look target before draw() moves the figure onto the floor (`stand`). A grounded figure can therefore look past a nearby object with no warning. The reference scene three-point-landing reports "gaze short of target by 7 deg" for this reason.

## Task
For scene v2, finish support placement before solving gaze. Report the angle between the final head-forward vector and the vector from the final eye point to the target (undefined for coincident points). Keep v1 drawings unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
Two grounded figures of different heights looking at a nearby parcel report errors that match an independent measurement from the exported transforms, impossible turns included.

## Tests
The fixture above; existing goldens unchanged.

## Context
lib/pose/mannequin.js: fig() and draw().

## Plan reference
Plan section 5.2

title: Shared sets and camera setups for reverse angles
description:
## Background
Reverse angles must keep the same window, door and light direction.

## Task
Add shared set revisions (floor, axes, fixed props, landmarks and light sources, all in set coordinates), camera setups that reference a set, and boards that reference a setup. Resolve all of them to the same geometry before projection, and include their digests in the board receipt.

## Acceptance criteria
Moving the shared window once moves it, and the key light, in a wide, a reverse and a return shot.

## Tests
That fixture.

## Context
child-peek repeats its corner, wall and window by hand in every scene file; it should become the first shared set.

## Plan reference
Plan sections 5.1 and 5.2

title: Fixed camera basics: vertical field of view and delivery frame size
description:
## Background
Scene records always auto-fit the figure into a 320 x 200 frame, so a camera can't stay put across shots and portrait boards are impossible.

## Task
Add a fixed perspective camera selected by camera.verticalFovDeg, and a per-scene frame size {w,h}, keeping auto-fit as the default.

## Acceptance criteria
The child-peek boards render in portrait with fixed cameras, and the existing goldens are unchanged.

## Context
lib/pose/mannequin.js, lib/pose/README.md.

## Plan reference
Plan section 8, order 3
close_reason: Done in commit 9d50111: camera.verticalFovDeg selects a fixed perspective camera via the sh.fix path in draw(); frame {w,h} sets the frame size per scene (default 320 x 200), reset after each render. Documented in lib/pose/README.md. All 45 tests pass with goldens unchanged; the child-peek boards render at 180 x 320 with fixed cameras. Hardening and its tests stay in am-e-board-1wg.8.

title: Draw street props for child-peek: scooter with rider and box, car, streetlight, kerb and parking bay, headlight
description:
## Background
child-peek's shot list asks for things the renderer can't draw: in sh4 the scooter is drawn as a man sitting on a box, and sh3 has no corner, streetlight or headlight, so neither board meets its must-see. am-mcd.15 also needs an empty parking bay in sh1. The full environment presets (am-e-board-1wg.4) are phase B; this bead is the minimum for phase A.

## Task
Add prop types to the scene record's props (expanded like the existing props), drawn in the sketch style and depth-sorted with figures: a scooter (two wheels, body, handlebars) with a seated rider pose and a square box on a rear rack; a small car silhouette; a streetlight (post, arm, lamp); a kerb line and painted parking-bay lines on the ground plane; and a headlight as a lamp point with an optional beam wedge (the value pass, am-00y.2, shades it later). Document each in lib/pose/README.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- At phone thumbnail size, a fresh viewer names the scooter, the box, the streetlight and the empty parking bay.
- Existing goldens are unchanged.

## Tests
Golden render per prop; a child-peek board using each one.

title: Clip board drawing to the frame border
description:
## Background
In the child-peek boards (sh2, sh3, sh5) the balusters, legs and rail run past the bottom frame line, so the frame no longer contains the picture.

## Task
Clip all drawing except the frame border and its sketch overshoots to the frame rectangle (an SVG clipPath is enough). Keep the border's deliberately overshooting lines.

## Acceptance criteria
No stroke apart from the border crosses the frame in any child-peek board; any change to the reference goldens is reviewed with test/golden-review.js before they are updated.

## Tests
A golden with a limb crossing the frame edge.

title: Warn when limbs pass through the body, each other or props
description:
## Background
A pose can be legal in numbers and still wrong on paper.

## Task
Build capsules for limb segments and torso parts, and boxes and bars for props. Report overlaps beyond a tolerance, excluding intended contacts.

## Acceptance criteria
Hands on a rail and sitting on a box don't warn; a forearm through the chest does.

## Tests
Unit tests for both cases.

## Plan reference
Plan section 7, step 6

title: Move renderer state into a per-render context, then split modules
description:
## Background
mannequin.js keeps mutable module state (P, GS, HS, BL, EX, FACE, CLAMPS, rnd, plus W and H for the frame size, which renderFrame resets in a finally block). Render order can therefore change the output, and several figures per frame aren't safe.

## Task
First move all mutable state into a context created per render. Then split the file into math, shapes, skeleton, render and api modules with readable names. No change in behaviour.

## Acceptance criteria
The golden tests pass byte for byte; frames rendered in any order match; the public API (renderFrame, renderSheet, renderLineup, PROFILES, LIMITS, FRAME) is unchanged.

## Tests
The golden tests plus the existing order-shuffling test.

## Context
lib/pose/mannequin.js (about 1,250 lines). The warning tests (am-e-tool-toz.2) must land first.

## Plan reference

title: Add environment presets: ground, rooms, cuboid buildings, doors, windows

title: Harden the fixed camera: near-plane clipping, straight-down view, locked-marker test
description:
## Background
The fixed camera exists already (see am-e-board-1wg.16, commit 9d50111). camera.verticalFovDeg switches a scene from auto-fit to a fixed perspective camera; frame {w,h} sets the frame size; and draw() uses the same fixed scale-and-offset path as renderLineup (sh.fix). What's missing are the parts needed once cameras go inside rooms or look straight down, plus tests that prove the camera is really fixed.

## Task
- Clip primitives that cross the near plane, instead of projecting them from behind the lens.
- Use a usable up vector when the camera looks straight down or straight up.
- Decide whether to add an explicit `mode: "fixed"` field or keep "verticalFovDeg present" as the switch, and document the choice in lib/pose/README.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- A locked camera keeps a world marker on the same pixel while the subject moves.
- A figure moved across a fixed frame changes position and size.
- Portrait and landscape frames render without stretching.
- Near-plane crossings are clipped.
- Existing goldens are unchanged.

## Tests
Centre-to-edge translation; distance scaling; a vertical camera; a near-plane crossing.

## Context
lib/pose/mannequin.js: toInternal(), draw(). Used by examples/child-peek/scenes/.

title: Check visibility where forms overlap, replacing per-box depth bias
description:
## Background
draw() sorts each form by a single average depth, so a big form can paint over a small one that's really in front of it. child-peek works around this with hand-tuned `bias` values on its wall (60), window (30) and slab (5) boxes. That is a hack and won't scale to presets or several figures.

## Task
- Keep stable part and prop ids through geometry expansion.
- For occlusion-critical regions, compare camera-space depth along shared camera rays using simple surface proxies, and correct the drawing order or split the form where the order changes.
- Flag disagreements for review; never accept them automatically.
- Once this works, remove the bias values from child-peek.

## Acceptance criteria
- In a crossing-bars fixture, the visible part switches at the known crossing.
- Both ladder views agree with the drawn overlaps.
- child-peek renders correctly with every bias removed.

## Tests
A crossing-bars fixture; visibility of hand-labelled points; child-peek goldens.

title: Build a sound-effects and foley library with provenance
description:
## Background
Storyboard films carry their reality in sound: a car that is heard but not seen, footsteps, a door, a room's ambience. child-peek needs two effects; phase B and later films need many, and they must be found, licensed and reused consistently.

## Task
- A library folder of effects and foley (performed, synced sounds such as footsteps, cloth and handling) plus ambience beds, each stored by digest with a provenance record (source, author, licence, or recorded by the producer), tags (what, where, distance, intensity), duration and loudness.
- Shots or beats request sounds by tag and timing (a speech cue or picture anchor plus offset), resolved to a library entry. The mix places, fades and ducks them with the music bed under the narration.
- Start from owned recordings and CC0 sources. Record anything commercially licensed with its licence terms. Never pull an asset without provenance into the edit.

## Acceptance criteria
- child-peek's two effects come from the library by tag.
- A phase B film's sound list resolves entirely from the library, or reports the missing entries.
- Assembly refuses an effect with incomplete provenance.

## Tests
Resolution by tag; missing-entry report; provenance refusal.

title: Build the minimal compiler: stills, hard cuts and voice to MP4
description:
## Background

## Task

- Reject empty or reversed intervals. Check the media bytes against their digests before assembling.
- Call FFmpeg with argument arrays: stills held for their spans, hard cuts, PCM voice plus an optional effects track, H.264 and AAC in MP4. Check the FFmpeg version and the needed filters at startup.

## Acceptance criteria
A playable child-peek MP4 in which each change of angle lands on its marked cue frame.

## Tests
Decode the frames either side of each cut; duration matches the audio sample count within one frame.

Inputs: am-mcd.2 (voice and marks) and am-mcd.3 (boards).
